viNames.name: Cá Phượng Hoàng Ngũ Sắc Lùn (balloon form)

origin.fact: It is a colour morph of the ram cichlid, Mikrogeophagus ramirezi, and was developed in 2009. The developer is not named.
It became widely known around 2009. It arose from selective breeding plus a chance mutation.
Farmed blue rams come mainly from Eastern Europe and Southeast Asia.
Wild rams come from the llanos of the Orinoco basin in Venezuela and Colombia.

looks.fact: The whole body is a bright metallic blue and the eyes are red.
The scales are electric blue with black and yellow-orange spots. The dorsal and tail fins are often yellow-orange.
Males have a slightly longer dorsal fin, but sexing is very hard.

lines.fact: Balloon electric blue ram: a short, rounded body form.
In Vietnam the balloon form is sold as Phượng Hoàng Ngũ Sắc Lùn.
Longfin balloon electric blue ram: the balloon body with long fins.
Powder blue ram: reportedly made by crossing electric blue with gold rams and keeping the palest blue young. It is doubtful whether it breeds true.

keeping.fact: Allow about 75 L (20 US gal) for one pair and at least 150 L (40 US gal) for two pairs. Do not put them in a newly set-up tank.
They are sensitive to nitrate and organic waste. They need good filtration, gentle flow and regular water changes.
Give them dense plants, open swimming space, caves and flat stones.
They eat both meaty and plant foods. Newly moved fish may refuse food, and mosquito larvae can tempt them to eat.
Avoid fast, aggressive tankmates and other dwarf cichlids. Use slow, peaceful companions.
Pencilfish and tetras are suggested tankmates. Keep them away from other cichlids.
Change 20-30% of the water weekly. Feed 2-3 times a day.

breeding.fact: They form monogamous pairs, and both parents guard the eggs and fry. Buying a group of juveniles is the cheapest way to get a pair.
They spawn on flat stones. Eggs hatch in about 40 hours, and the fry swim freely at about 5 days.
Colour morphs are less fertile and worse at brood care than wild-type rams. Young pairs often eat their eggs.
Two blue rams usually breed true.
One forum poster says the electric blue gene is incompletely dominant. Crossing it with gold gives young with only a slight blue tint.
One breeder crossed electric blue with gold and got mixed-colour young.

health.fact: Reports suggest blue and other exaggerated morphs catch disease more easily than normal rams, and whitespot is a particular weakness. Keep a whitespot treatment on hand.
Fish given hormones are weaker and live shorter lives.
Common problems are fungus, whitespot, fin rot and skin flukes. Quarantine new fish for 1-2 weeks.

buying.fact: Buy from a trusted dealer or breeder. Avoid fish that are unusually cheap, since they may have been given hormones.
Pick fish with bright colour that swim actively and show no signs of disease. Check that the shop's water is clean.
Vietnamese prices quoted: juveniles 30,000-50,000 VND, pairs 200,000-300,000 VND.
One Vietnamese shop listed them at 100,000 VND.

controversy.fact: Practical Fishkeeping says some fish are given hormones to boost their colour. The colour can fade later, leaving a weaker fish.
Practical Fishkeeping says these demanding fish are often sold to beginners who keep them in tanks that are too small or not yet established.
TFH warns that cheap, hormone-treated fish are weakened and short-lived.
